$comment: Machine-readable Datum Labs brand spec, transcribed from 'Datum Labs - Brand Expansion' (2026). This file is the single source of truth for scripts/brand-lint.ts. Update it here, never in the linter.

electric-sapphire.use: The action colour. Links, primary fills, the brandmark.

prussian-blue.use: Deepest ink. Type and inverse surfaces.

navy.use: Depth under Electric Sapphire; gradient end stop.

onyx.$unverified: The deck prints Onyx as #000B78 — identical to Navy — which is a copy error, since the swatch is clearly near-black. #141414 is a stand-in read from the swatch. Replace with the real value.

neutrals.$comment: Derived from Prussian Blue and Platinum, not given in the deck. Needed for UI states the brand book does not cover.

dataPalette.$comment: NOT brand colours. A categorical scale for encoding sector, which the brand book does not address and a directory cannot work without. Governed here so the linter can allow exactly these and nothing else.

primary.$comment: The deck says 'Source Serif Pro'; Google Fonts now ships it as Source Serif 4. Same typeface, current name.

gradients.rule: Gradients are core to the identity, but only approved ones. Build them from tokens — never from raw hex — so a palette change cannot leave a gradient behind.
gradients.recipe: Brandmark silhouette, then noise (mono, #000B78 at 20%), texture, and layer blur. Noise for depth, texture for tactility, blur for a soft finish.

texture.rule: Dashed intersecting lines over colour gradients, soft-light blend. Adds depth without competing with the palette beneath.

imagery.rule: Custom dithering, blue duotone. No plain photography.

lint.$comment: Token files declare the palette, so they are the source of truth rather than a violation of it.
lint.$emailComment: lib/email/templates.ts uses literal hex on purpose: email clients do not support CSS custom properties. The literals must still be brand values, so the linter checks them like anything else.

statusPalette.$comment: Also not brand colours. Success/warning/danger are functional signals the brand book does not cover, and a product that reviews submissions and sends email cannot work without them. Kept deliberately desaturated so they sit under the blue rather than fight it.

derived.$comment: Stepped from Prussian Blue and Platinum. The brand book gives five colours; a working interface needs a neutral ramp for borders, muted type and sunken surfaces. Declared here so the linter knows them, and so anything outside this ramp is still a violation.
